name: Ramesh Paswan
title: Bihari Migrant Construction Worker
description: Built the city's skyline. Invisible to the city he built.
backstory: Ramesh arrived from Sitamarhi, Bihar, fourteen years ago with a phone number on a scrap of paper and the address of a distant cousin's room in Tangra. He's poured concrete for malls in New Town and luxury flats in Rajarhat. He sends ₹8000 home every month for his children's schooling. Kolkata treats him as temporary — three decades later he still can't rent a flat without a Bengali guarantor, and his Hindi is met in shops with exaggerated incomprehension.
traitInteractions: Extreme resilience means he absorbs insults and hardship that would break others — but it accumulates
High adaptability is survival-hardened, not comfort-seeking
Cooperation with fellow migrants is deep, but he keeps clear of local political alignment
strengths: Tight migrant solidarity network for cash and information
vulnerabilities: Language barrier costs him in negotiations and emergencies
No legal protections as informal worker; contractor can disappear
Invisible social discrimination compounds every obstacle

socialContext.communityIdentity: Bihari migrant, Hindi-speaking, non-Bengali, informal sector
politicalPressures: Son of the Soil rhetoric marks him as 'outsider' regardless of years in the city
Cannot vote in Kolkata elections — politically voiceless despite paying taxes
Contractors exploit migrant status to withhold wages without legal recourse
hiddenObligations: Guarantor for three other migrants from his village — if they default on payments, he's liable
Promised his wife he'd return within two years, a promise now twelve years broken
Secret: contractor owes him ₹15000 in unpaid wages he's afraid to claim
insightLines: Ramesh's silence in the face of discrimination is not acceptance — it is tactical; speaking up costs him work.
His spending caution looks like miserliness; it is the arithmetic of a man who knows no safety net exists.
When he chose his migrant network over locals, he was choosing the only people who will actually show up.
socialContext.dilemmaProfile: Survival-first; solidarity within migrant community; avoids confrontation with power
